findings.issue: P123.88 asked for the rule of the CLASS (any long unbroken token in any text surface the report prints). The rule is a list of five elements under .content (p, li, dd, summary, blockquote), not the class. A render of the live plan shows the same worktree/branch token (audit/p109-...) also inside div.pmeta and span elements, and headings, divs and spans outside a table are not covered; .pmeta (gate-rail.css:60, shell.css:95) has no overflow-wrap of its own. Whether that div sits inside a scrolling .tablewrap on the live plan was not driven in a browser (browser gates were kept out of this review), so no overflow is demonstrated, only an uncovered surface of the same shape. The only test is u14k, a source-string pin on the rule (test_render_report.py:340); the task's gate runs the interactive checker on the acme-store example, which never overflowed, so nothing in the gate would catch the live-plan regression returning.
findings.resolution: Move the rule from an element list to the container (overflow-wrap:anywhere on .content, with :where() tables/pre excluded if their min-content sizing must stay) so it covers every text element, or name in the CSS comment why headings, div and span are safe. Add a case that renders a plan with a long unbroken token in a phase title, a finding and a worktree note and runs the 320px check, so the class is proved and not just the string.

findings.issue: lock_to_give_back now calls dispatch_out -> load_phase -> _mio.load_manifest, which sits OUTSIDE drive()'s try/except. dispatch_out catches only ValueError; load_manifest raises OSError for a plan or shard that vanished or became unreadable between drive_locked's own read and this one. The exception then surfaces as a traceback with the phase lock still taken and recorded in state, the stranded-lock shape the desired outcome rules out. The window is small, but this predicate is the only place on the lock-release path that reads the plan a second time.
findings.resolution: In dispatch_out catch (ValueError, OSError) and return False (release), or move the lock_to_give_back call inside the same try that already releases on BaseException. Add a dl case with the plan removed between the refusal and the predicate.

findings.issue: _PULL_ARG_SHORTS = "sXoj" omits -S (git pull --gpg-sign[=<keyid>] takes an attached key id), so in a cluster such as -Sr the r is the key id but is read as the rebase flag, a false history-rewrite breach of the same class P123.85 closed. The cluster test also needs t[1:].isalpha(), so a cluster that contains -4/-6 (e.g. -4r) is not seen at all. Both are rare and the resolution text allowed the cluster to be a documented non-goal.
findings.resolution: Add S to _PULL_ARG_SHORTS (and a clean rw9 row such as -Sr), or state in the docstring that digits and -S are unread.
